# The Catalog vs CogPO

[CogPO](http://www.cogpo.org/), the Cognitive Paradigm Ontology, and the Catalog both
name experimental paradigms and both refuse to define a paradigm by the mental process
it is supposed to measure. From there they diverge. CogPO describes a paradigm by its
observable components, the stimuli, responses and instructions, so that an imaging
experiment can be coded. The Catalog names standard tasks, tests membership by
procedure, and links each task to the processes it engages, so that a dataset can be
tagged. Each has what the other lacks.

[What is CogPO?](what_is_cogpo.md) describes CogPO on its own terms. The
[paradigm mapping](paradigm_mapping.md) page gives the correspondence between the two
paradigm lists row by row, the [dimension mapping](dimension_mapping.md) page sets
CogPO's stimulus, response and instruction vocabularies beside the Catalog's facets and
the HED schema, and the [CogPO mapping method](../methods/cogpo_mapping_method.md) page
explains how each row was decided. This page says what it adds up to.

## Two resources doing different jobs

CogPO was built for BrainMap, a database of coordinate-based neuroimaging results. Its
job is to let a curator code a published experiment so that experiments can be compared
and pooled: which paradigm classes apply, what the participant saw, did and was told in
each condition. Hence the "in at least one of the conditions" clause in every
definition, the instruction to co-code overlapping classes, and a paradigm list that
includes acupuncture, breath holding and chewing beside Stroop and n-back. Anything an
imaging study might do had to be codable.

The Catalog was built for HED annotation of event-structured data. Its job is to give a
dataset a task name that carries a stable meaning: a procedure that can be recognized, a
set of processes that a reader can expect the events to bear on, and a list of the
variations that keep the name. Hence the inclusion tests, the variation rules, the
references and the process axis, and the exclusion of procedures with no trial
structure.

The difference in scale is smaller than with the Cognitive Atlas, because both resources
are curated lists rather than open contributions.

|  | The Catalog | CogPO |
|---|---|---|
| Experimental paradigms | 103 tasks and 4 pseudo tasks | 83 classes (84 on the wiki) |
| Cognitive processes | 172 | not modelled |
| Named variations | {{ n_variations }} | not modelled |
| Stimulus, response and instruction vocabularies | facets, seeded from CogPO | 6 vocabularies, about 100 values |
| References per paradigm | curated, with roles | occasional BrainMap citation on a definition |
| Last curated | ongoing | 2011 |

## Where they agree

Both put procedure first. A CogPO paradigm class is defined by what the participant sees
and does, never by the construct it is claimed to tap, and the Catalog's inclusion tests
do the same. The 27 exact matches are the paradigms that any list of standard cognitive
tasks converges on, and their definitions in the two resources describe the same
procedure in different words.

Both split the paradigm from its response modality only when the field does. CogPO has
overt and covert classes for naming, reading, repetition, word generation and word stem
completion, because in an fMRI scanner the difference between saying a word and thinking
it is the difference between two experiments; the Catalog treats the response as a
variation. Neither treats the response modality as making a new task anywhere else.

## Where they differ

**Process axis.** CogPO has none. The Catalog's 172 processes and its task-process links
have no counterpart, and nothing in CogPO says that the Stroop task engages selective
attention and interference control. This is the largest difference and it is by design:
CogPO left "what is measured" to BrainMap's separate behavioral-domain taxonomy.

**Scope.** 36 CogPO classes have no counterpart in the Catalog. Fifteen are paradigms the
Catalog could list and does not: Braille reading, deception, counting or calculation,
divided auditory attention, film viewing, motor imagery, visual imagery, music
comprehension or production, olfactory discrimination, overt reading, covert and overt
recitation, video games, and covert and overt word stem completion. Eleven are
physiological procedures or interventions (acupuncture, breath holding, chewing, eating,
micturition, sleep, TMS, electrical, thermal, painful and vibrotactile stimulation), six
are motor acts (grasping, pointing, drawing, writing, whistling, flexion or extension),
three are broad perceptual classes and one is the flashing checkerboard. The Catalog's
task criteria exclude the last four groups deliberately.

In the other direction, 35 of the Catalog's 107 tasks have no CogPO class at all and 26
more fall only under a broad class such as Reward Task or Visual Attention. CogPO has no
economic games, no metacognition, no priming, no spatial navigation, no implicit
learning, no complex span, no stop-signal and no questionnaire.

**Broad classes.** Ten CogPO classes are families rather than paradigms: Encoding,
Episodic Recall, Reward Task, Semantic Discrimination, Visual Distractor/Visual
Attention (CogPO's own word for it is "catch-all"), Face Monitor or Discrimination and
their kin. Nine Catalog reward tasks fall under Reward Task Paradigm alone. Where the
Catalog has a specific task inside such a class, the row is `close`; where it has only
neighbours, `related`.

**Variations, inclusion tests, references.** CogPO has none of the three.

## What CogPO adds

The dimension vocabularies. CogPO is the only one of the resources compared on this site
that says, in a closed vocabulary, what a participant is shown, what they do with which
body part, and what they are told to do. The Catalog has needed exactly this since its
facets were first planned, and it adopts CogPO's six vocabularies as the starting point
for its stimulus, response and instruction facets, crediting every value to CogPO in
`data/facet_defs.tsv` and marking every addition. The
[dimension mapping](dimension_mapping.md) page lists the values, the additions and the
few values dropped as out of scope.

## CogPO and the HED schema

CogPO's dimensions are close kin to the HED schema: each of the six lands in one HED
subtree, and 88 of the 102 CogPO values have a HED 8.4.0 tag. That kinship is why the
Catalog can adopt CogPO's vocabularies as facets without inventing a parallel one, and
why a facet value on a task can become a tag on the dataset's events.
[HED vs CogPO](hed_vs_cogpo.md) sets the two out in full: what each describes, where the
vocabularies meet value by value, and what each has that the other lacks.

## What the comparison changes

For the Catalog, CogPO is a source of vocabulary more than of paradigms. The fifteen
task-shaped classes the Catalog lacks are candidates for the issue tracker, not
omissions: most describe imaging-era block designs (film viewing, overt reading,
recitation) whose event structure is thin. The dimension vocabularies, by contrast, go
straight into the facets.

For a reader of CogPO, the Catalog supplies what CogPO left out: a process layer,
variations, inclusion tests and references for the 50 classes the two share, and, for
the classes CogPO never populated, the paradigm-to-dimension assignments that its design
called for and its curation never reached.
